review.headline: Punishing Early Queen Excursions

sections.text: White brought their queen out on move two and continued to hunt for quick threats, playing 8.Qc4 and 9.Qb3. Rather than panicking, you castled queenside and coordinated your forces while White lagged behind in development.
When White's queen got misplaced on a3, pinning your d6-pawn to e7, you stabilized cleanly with 12...b6! and struck in the center with 13...d5.

White blundered with 18.Nxd4?, and you seized the moment with 18...Nxb4!, executing a discovered attack by the queen on d7 against the knight on d4. After winning a piece with 20...Bxd4+ and forcing a series of trades, you entered a completely winning endgame.
You activated your rooks and knight smoothly in the final phase. White tried a desperate raid on your c-pawn, but your pieces swarmed the exposed king to deliver mate with 33...R8d2#.

review.turning_point: White's 18.Nxd4? walked into the tactical strike 18...Nxb4!, winning material and simplifying directly into a decisive endgame.
review.focus: Look for immediate central counterstrikes when an opponent moves their queen early: 8...d5 would have punished 8.Qc4 instantly instead of the passive 8...Qd7.
